A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CycleQD work. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated related work and renumbered figures.

before.justification: v1 reports original CycleQD experiments on computer-science tasks, component ablations, generalization benchmarks, and image segmentation, including Tables 1–4.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds NSGA-II comparison results, joint VQA/computer-science results, and performance-versus-generation and training-time findings.

M1.justification: The cyclic archive updates, elite sampling, crossover, SVD mutation, and aggregation remain unchanged. The VQA experiment applies these operations to the extracted Llama3 component of a vision-language model. The added explanation that crossover weights can be negative clarifies the existing Gaussian sampling rule.

E1.justification: Appendix A.1.5 adds TextVQA expert training and joint optimization/evaluation with coding, DB, and OS tasks. This extends combined skill acquisition to image-conditioned question answering, beyond the previously separate language-agent and image-segmentation experiments. Existing dataset and task coverage is retained.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds an evaluated NSGA-II model-merging baseline, which optimizes multiple objectives simultaneously. The existing fine-tuning, averaging, gradient-based merging, and CMA-ES comparators remain.

E3.justification: The new VQA experiment specifies a Llama3-LLaVA-NeXT-8B expert trained on 4,000 samples, with 500 separate samples divided equally between CycleQD optimization and testing, using 1,200 generations. Appendix A.1.3 also evaluates performance every 100 generations. These are added protocols; previously stated experimental settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix A.1.3 adds a search-duration analysis showing average task performance across generations and stabilization around 1,000 generations. This supplements the retained archive-development snapshots. The original component ablations and segmentation case analyses are unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports uncertainty intervals, significance tests, or repeated-seed estimates for the performance comparisons. The unchanged three-run QD ablation uses different quality objectives, rather than reporting statistical replication. The new convergence plot adds no uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Existing scores in Tables 1–4 are retained, but substantial results are added. NSGA-II averages 51.6 versus CycleQD's unchanged 52.4 in Table 1. Under the new four-task setting, Table 5 reports CycleQD scores of 54.1 VQA, 72.9 MBPP, 32.4 DB, and 39.6 OS, averaging 49.7. The convergence curve and approximately 410 versus 200 GPU-hour comparison add further outcomes.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and formulas for archives, sampling, crossover, mutation, aggregation, and model similarity are unchanged. The new preliminaries and expanded explanations introduce no substantive mathematical derivation, assumption, theorem, or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution bullets, and conclusion retain the claims of effective multi-skill merging, competitive agent performance, preserved language capabilities, and applicability beyond language models. Reduced tuning effort was already a central motivation. The VQA experiment supplies additional support for existing breadth claims.

C2.justification: v2 adds an explanation contrasting CycleQD's cyclic diversity mechanism with NSGA-II, interprets the existing ablations as component synergy, and discusses computational limitations. Appendix A.1.7 attributes runtime mainly to agent evaluations and notes CPU merging caused by GPU-memory constraints. The original expert-compatibility limitation remains.

D1.justification: v2 newly discloses preliminary short-run hyperparameter selection, NVIDIA H100 hardware, CPU-side merging, and training times, explicitly excluding expert training from CycleQD's 410 GPU-hours. It also documents the VQA model and sample allocation. These extend reproducibility information without changing the previously reported hyperparameter values or code-access link.

R1.justification: v2 adds references for NSGA-II and TextVQA and explicitly attributes elite-sampling inspiration to Wang et al. (2023), previously cited more generally. It also discusses CycleQD relative to NSGA-II. The original detailed related-work discussion survives in Appendix B rather than being removed.

P1.justification: The narrative is substantially reorganized: a new Section 2 introduces evolutionary strategies and MAP-Elites, the former related-work section moves to Appendix B, and a condensed related-work section appears before the conclusion. Method explanations and the ablation discussion are expanded, and the appendix gains new subsections.

P2.justification: v2 adds the MAP-Elites flow diagram, generation-performance curve, and VQA results table, and expands Table 1 with an NSGA-II row. Figure 1 and several displays are resized or repositioned. These are bounded additions within the retained visual design; the existing SVD, archive, and segmentation figures are preserved.

improvement.justification: The relevant NSGA-II comparison, explicit computational costs, VQA experiment, and convergence analysis make performance and applicability better supported and easier to assess. The reorganized background also improves accessibility. These are useful incremental gains: the main results remain unchanged, and uncertainty reporting still does not establish the reliability of the narrow 52.4 versus 51.6 advantage.
